newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Lone Japanese dealer lifts Singapore rubber.
newsitem.headline: Lone Japanese dealer lifts Singapore rubber.

text.p: A single Japanese dealer engaged in a buying spree on Friday to take advantage of the arbitrage between the Singapore and Tokyo rubber markets, providing joy to producers, dealers said.
"It was one speculator. He was buying at such a good price across the board. There are quite a lot of people who were very happy at the prices he offered," a dealer said.

"The buying was arbitrage-related. He was obviously playing the arbitrage of his positions between the Singapore market and the one in Tokyo," another dealer said. The buying boosted prices of RSS3 and RSS1 grade rubber by up to four cents.
Dealers said the bulk of the buying by the Japanese dealer was in the morning session and reached about 5,000 tonnes.
"There was some more light buying in the afternoon by other players in the market, but it was relatively quiet by then because it's Friday," a trader said.

At 0945 GMT, June RSS3 prices jumped sharply and were seen at 114.00 U.S. cents a kg from yesterday's close of 111.75 cents. July RSS3 climbed to 115.00 U.S. cents a kg from 113.25 cents. June RSS1 prices also went up and were seen at 165.25 Singapore cents (US$1.15) a kg from 161.25 cents.
